title: The property of being a henselian pair is preserved by limits
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that an inverse limit of henselian pairs, with the limit ideal, is again a henselian pair. The proof reduces to products and equalizers since limits in the relevant category are built from those, quotes the product case, and then treats an equalizer diagram of henselian pairs. The verification uses Gabber's criterion: elements of one plus the limit ideal are units because inverses are unique and the statement holds in the first pair, which puts the limit ideal inside the Jacobson radical, and then a polynomial of the shape used in the criterion, whose coefficients apart from the leading ones lie in the limit ideal, has a unique root near one in the first ring, whose images under the two parallel maps agree by uniqueness, so that root descends to the equalizer.
